text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Run-off polls set for April 3 in 111 local council areas out of 774 in which municipal elections were held two weeks ago.
- Power and steel minister Bashir Dalhatu says state electricity utility NEPA needs 2.4 billion naira to solve the problem of constant power cuts.
- No duty will be charged on goods coming into Nigeria for exhibition at Africa trade fair scheduled to start in the north on Saturday, says fair organising committee chairman Tukur Mani.
- National Clearing and Forwarding Agency, a government company, lays off 50 staff in last one month following major reorganistion ordered by the military government.
- Job queues lengthen as 115 companies close shop in second half of last year, says manufacturers association in half-year report.
- Two more buildings razed in oil town of Warri in protest riots over relocation of a local government headquarters that led villagers to take staff of Shell hostages.
- Finance minister Anthony Ani lists seven steps he says can lead to accelerated socio-economic growth for Nigeria by the year 2000.
- British Labour Party, which is favoured to win general elections in May, will soon spell out its policy on Nigeria's political crisis, a party official tells newspaper in London.
- Major oil marketing companies lose 2.3 billion naira from recent fuel shortage in Lagos and environs.
